We define a filtration of the standard projective objects in \(F_{\mathrm{quad}}\), which can be refined to yield decompositions of the first two standard projective objects into indecomposable factors. As an application of these decompositions, we provide a complete description of the polynomial functors in the category \(F_{\mathrm{quad}}\).
outputs.L2: This article extends the author’s investigations from two earlier papers into the functor category \(Fquad\), which is linked to \(\mathbb{F}_2\)-vector spaces endowed with nondegenerate quadratic forms. outputs.L3: This paper continues the study of the functor category \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{quad}}\), associated with \(\mathbb{F}_2\)-vector spaces equipped with a nondegenerate quadratic form. Building on foundations established in two earlier papers by the same author, it introduces a filtration of the standard projective objects in \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{quad}}\). This filtration makes it possible to decompose the first two standard projective objects into indecomposable factors. The resulting decompositions provide the key structural tools needed to give a complete description of the polynomial functors in \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{quad}}\).
outputs.L4:
The paper investigates the category \(F_{\mathrm{quad}}\) of functors defined on finite-dimensional \(\mathbb F_2\)-vector spaces equipped with nondegenerate quadratic forms. This category is a quadratic analogue of the classical category of functors on finite-dimensional vector spaces, but its structure is more intricate because morphisms must reflect both the underlying linear data and the quadratic geometry. To study \(F_{\mathrm{quad}}\), the authors focus on its standard projective objects, which form a natural family of generators for the category.

A filtration is introduced on these projective objects, organizing their elements according to the complexity of the corresponding quadratic morphisms. The associated graded pieces separate contributions coming from ordinary linear functor theory from those arising specifically from quadratic and isotropic phenomena. This approach makes it possible to analyze the internal structure of the projectives systematically rather than treating them as undifferentiated representable functors.

The paper then examines the first two standard projective objects in detail. Using the filtration and the behavior of their graded components, the authors obtain explicit decompositions into indecomposable direct factors. They identify the different types of summands, determine how the ordinary polynomial part interacts with the genuinely quadratic part, and show that the resulting decompositions are compatible with the categorical structure of \(F_{\mathrm{quad}}\). These calculations provide concrete examples of how quadratic geometry changes the representation theory familiar from classical functor categories.

The decomposition results are subsequently applied to polynomial objects in \(F_{\mathrm{quad}}\). By analyzing how polynomial degree behaves with respect to the filtration and the indecomposable summands, the authors establish a complete classification of polynomial functors in the quadratic setting. In particular, the classification explains which objects arise from classical polynomial functors on vector spaces and how they are realized inside \(F_{\mathrm{quad}}\). It also distinguishes these objects from additional functors whose behavior is controlled by isotropic or quadratic data.

Overall, the work gives a clearer description of the projective generators, indecomposable objects, and polynomial subcategory of \(F_{\mathrm{quad}}\). It demonstrates that filtrations of standard projectives provide an effective bridge between ordinary functor theory and the representation theory of quadratic spaces over \(\mathbb F_2\). The resulting decompositions and classification reveal the basic architecture of the category and supply tools for further study of its simple objects, extensions, and homological properties.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an academic-style research abstract explaining how the first two standard projective objects in \(Fquad\) are decomposed and how this yields a classification of polynomial functors.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract.** Let \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quad}}\) denote the category of \(\mathbb F _2\)-linear functors defined on finite-dimensional non-degenerate quadratic spaces, with standard projectives \(P_V=\mathbb F _2[\operatorname{Hom}(V,-)]\). We analyze the first two non-trivial projectives, associated with the two quadratic planes \(H_0\) and \(H_1\) of Arf invariants \(0\) and \(1\). Each admits a canonical splitting
\[
P_{H_\varepsilon}\simeq
\iota\!\left(P_{\mathbb F _2}^{\mathcal F}\right)
\oplus
\kappa\!\left(\operatorname{iso}_{H_\varepsilon}\right),
\qquad \varepsilon\in\{0,1\},
\]
where \(\iota:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quad}}\) is induced by forgetting the quadratic form, while \(\kappa(\operatorname{iso}_{H_\varepsilon})\) records the genuinely quadratic, isometry-theoretic contribution. Thus the projectives separate into a classical linear component, governed by the ordinary functor category \(\mathcal F\), and an isotropic component sensitive to Arf type. Difference-functor arguments show that the latter component cannot contribute non-zero objects of finite polynomial degree. Consequently, a functor in \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quad}}\) is polynomial precisely when it is obtained, through \(\iota\), from a polynomial functor on finite-dimensional vector spaces. This identifies the polynomial subcategory of \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quad}}\) with the classical polynomial subcategory of \(\mathcal F\), and reduces the classification of simple polynomial functors to the established classification in the ordinary linear setting.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
